newsitem.title: USA: Report Clinton wants to restore welfare cuts. [CORRECTED 19:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Report Clinton wants to restore welfare cuts. [CORRECTED 19:55 GMT]

text.p: President Bill Clinton wants to revise the new welfare law to restore one-fourth of the $55 billion of the funds that would otherwise be saved over six years, The New York Times reported on Wednesday. (Corrects to add "one-fourth of...")

Quoting administration officials, the paper said the White House was contemplating restoration of food stamp eligibility for many legal immigrants who have not become citizens, a change from the new law that denies food stamps to noncitizens.
Another change, which would be submitted as part of a budget plan to be submitted to Congress in February, would increase food stamp allotments to families with high housing costs.
Another proposal being considered, the paper said, would relax some of the stringent work requirements for adults with dependents.

During the presidential campaign, Clinton urged voters to re-elect him so he could "fix" the law, which he signed Aug. 22. Republicans, who hold a majority in both houses of Congress, have said they have no interest in changing the law.
